summary.short: Italian bill (unified text C. 1928-A/R, pending in the Chamber of Deputies) delegating to the Government the power to adopt legislative decrees on data centres: construction permitting, grid access, energy, security, tax and cloud oversight, within six months of entry into force.
summary.long: The bill (unified text C. 1928-A/R, pending in the Chamber of Deputies) delegates to the Government the power to adopt one or more legislative decrees on data centres (centri di elaborazione dati) within six months of entry into force (Art. 3(1)). Art. 2 defines a data centre as the physical structure and technological infrastructure for designing, producing, developing and implementing IT applications and services and for storing, processing and managing the associated data. The delegated principles cover simplified, time-limited authorisation for construction, expansion and refurbishment; a dedicated ATECO code; single procedures; qualification of such projects as works of prevailing public interest with simplified environmental assessment (VIA) and integrated environmental authorisation (AIA); urban-planning simplification; priority grid access; on-site energy self-production and storage; national rules on diesel backup generator emissions; physical and cyber security; priority for reusing existing facilities with environmental efficiency; and tax harmonisation on permanent-establishment status. They also cover digital-skills training and expand the powers of the Autorità per le garanzie nelle comunicazioni over cloud services. Draft decrees need parliamentary opinions (Art. 3(3)) and new public charges are barred unless funded (Art. 3(4)-(5)). No penalty regime is stated.

notes: The bill is a delegation law: it states no legal basis and makes no operative amendment, repeal, implementation or transposition of another instrument. target_instrument_id is left empty because no registry IDs were supplied and the schema requires a string. Committee opinions cite earlier letter numbering for art. 3(1) ('ora lettera t)', 'lettera v)', 'lettera r)', 'lettera e)'); the unified text lists letters a) to i) and l) to s), with destinazione d'uso produttiva in lettera f) and stabile organizzazione in lettera o). The VIII Commission's proposed addition 'e direzionale' is not in the text. DPR 380/2001 and TUIR art. 162 appear only in committee opinions.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment appears in the operative provisions (Art. 1 to Art. 4). The numbers present are procedural time limits: six months for the delegated decrees (Art. 3(1)), sixty days for parliamentary opinions, and thirty, ninety and ten days (Art. 3(3)). These are deadlines, not thresholds. Art. 2 defines a data centre without a numeric cutoff. Any thresholds would be set later by the legislative decrees, which are not part of this text.
